title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Coverage
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare and say your coverage will be canceled unless you provide personal information or pay a fee. They may sound urgent and try to scare you.
example_message: "This is Medicare. Your coverage will be canceled unless you confirm your Social Security number and payment details right now."
red_flags: Caller asks for your Social Security number or bank info
Threatens to cancel your Medicare coverage
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you're concerned.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text saying a package couldn't be delivered and you need to click a link to reschedule or pay a fee. The link leads to a fake website that steals your information.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please click here to update your address and pay the $1.50 fee."
red_flags: Link asks for personal or payment info
what_to_do: Do not click the link; delete the message.

title: Social Security Email Phishing
how_it_works: You receive an email that looks like it's from the Social Security Administration, saying there's a problem with your account. The email asks you to click a link and enter your information.
example_message: "We have detected suspicious activity on your Social Security account. Please verify your information by clicking this link."
what_to_do: Do not click any links; contact Social Security using their official website or phone number.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: Someone calls pretending to be your grandchild or a lawyer, saying your grandchild is in trouble and needs money right away. They ask you not to tell anyone.
example_message: "Grandma, I’m in jail and need bail money. Please send $2,000 right away and don’t tell Mom and Dad."
red_flags: Says to keep it a secret
Wants payment by gift card, wire transfer, or cash
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member to check the story.

title: Facebook Marketplace Overpayment Scam
how_it_works: A buyer on Facebook Marketplace sends you a check for more than your item's price and asks you to send back the extra money. The check later bounces, and you lose the money you sent.
example_message: "I sent you $1,000 for your $600 item by mistake. Please send back the extra $400 via gift card."
red_flags: Buyer overpays and asks for a refund
Wants refund by gift card or wire transfer
Check comes from someone you don’t know
what_to_do: Never send money back to someone who overpays with a check.
